currentContext.expansion: SG Mart operates a pan-regional network of warehouses and service centres, with 7 operational service centres and 7,200+ SKUs as disclosed in the MD&A company overview. The Directors' Report states the Company plans to add three to four additional centres in FY27, with opportunities actively being evaluated in Hyderabad, Chennai and Punjab. Alongside the service centre build-out, the Company is expanding into application-led segments such as solar structures and steel profiles, and is undertaking backward integration initiatives including zinc coating to enhance value realisation. In the Steel Profiling Products vertical the stated intent is to scale capacity to 0.5 MTPA alongside further expansion of the distribution network and deeper engagement with channel partners, having transitioned that vertical from a trading-led model to a white-labelling and franchise-based royalty model with increased franchise onboarding during the year. In solar structures, the Company expanded its presence into rooftop solar structures and established a distribution network, operates in-house manufacturing capabilities across locations supported by advanced machinery and dedicated in-house tooling workshops, and aims to expand capacity up to 0.5 MTPA through ongoing capacity additions, scaling its presence significantly over the next two to three years. The MD&A strengths and opportunities commentary cites ongoing addition of service centres across geographies as an opportunity expected to improve volumes and operating leverage, and notes that a strong capital base supports expansion of service centres, capacity addition and working capital needs. Separately, the BRSR Principle 2 disclosure states the Company made capital investments in rainwater harvesting systems, alcohol breath analysers, fire safety equipment and water purification systems; such sustainability-linked capex was 0.04% of total capex in FY 2025-26 versus 0.2% in FY 2024-25. No rupee quantum for the overall capex programme is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

risks.note: Fluctuations in steel prices can lead to inventory losses, margin pressure and earnings volatility, particularly given the working capital-intensive nature of operations. The Company states that, as highlighted in recent performance, sharp corrections impacted EBITDA due to inventory holding cycles, and the MD&A notes margins were impacted during the period due to softness in demand and correction in steel prices. Mitigation cited: dynamic pricing, reduction in inventory holding cycles, and a greater contribution from higher-margin service centre and renewable structure segments.

risks.risk: Working capital intensity of an inventory-led trading model
risks.note: Listed as a weakness in the SWOT: inventory-led operations and supplier advances may impact return ratios if not tightly managed. The ratio commentary attributes lower debtors' and inventory turnover to higher trade receivables and higher average inventory during the year, compounding the exposure to price swings.

risks.risk: Increasing competition in a fragmented B2B construction-materials ecosystem
risks.note: The B2B ecosystem remains highly fragmented with increasing participation from organised platforms and digital aggregators, potentially exerting pressure on market share, pricing power and customer retention. Mitigation cited: continuous monitoring of competitive dynamics and pricing benchmarks, strengthening supplier relationships, widening the customer base and differentiating on standardised pricing, quality assurance and integrated supply solutions.

risks.risk: Digital disruption of the traditional trading model
risks.note: A gradual industry shift towards digital procurement platforms and organised marketplaces may reduce reliance on conventional trading models, impacting the long-term growth trajectory. Mitigation cited: shifting product mix towards value-added segments such as processing, distribution and specialty products, and strengthening platform-led capabilities.

risks.risk: Supply chain and logistics disruption, including supplier concentration
risks.note: The business model relies on seamless procurement and distribution of steel and construction materials; transportation constraints, supplier concentration or geopolitical factors may impact delivery timelines and operational efficiency. The BRSR materiality table reinforces this: as a trading and distribution business the Company does not control upstream production, so continuity of supply and its environmental and labour footprint depend heavily on third-party manufacturers and mills, and overreliance on a narrow supplier base creates both disruption and reputational risk.

Rapid expansion of service centres, product lines and geographies may lead to inefficiencies in inventory management, coordination challenges and execution risks, impacting service levels and margins. Mitigation cited: advanced inventory management systems, process standardisation, monitoring of operational KPIs and investment in logistics infrastructure and workforce capability.

risks.risk: Product quality, safety and standards compliance in traded construction materials
risks.note: Core trade is in structural and construction-grade steel products (TMT bars, HR coils/sheets, structural sections) alongside tiles, sanitaryware and electrical fittings. Because these are safety-critical, load-bearing or life-safety-relevant inputs, a certification or quality lapse at the manufacturer level can translate into construction-site safety risk and legal/reputational exposure for the Company as the distribution channel, even though it does not manufacture the goods. Mitigation cited: sourcing exclusively from BIS-certified and reputed brand manufacturers, quality verification at warehouses and service centres, and product traceability from source to dealer.

risks.risk: Talent capability and workforce stability against a lean employee base
risks.note: The BRSR materiality table states the Company operates with a comparatively lean corporate workforce relative to the scale and geographic spread of goods it moves, spanning commercial, supply-chain and finance functions; the MD&A reports a total of 177 employees as of March 31, 2026. As the Company grows and diversifies into new product categories, its ability to attract, train and retain capable talent is a key determinant of execution quality and growth sustainability.

risks.risk: Technological disruption and cyber risk in a platform-dependent model
risks.note: Dependence on digital platforms and IT infrastructure exposes operations to system failures, cyber threats and data integrity issues that could disrupt business continuity and stakeholder trust. Mitigation cited: IT governance frameworks, periodic system upgrades, cybersecurity protocols, real-time monitoring, regular audits, data backup and disaster recovery planning.

Demand is linked to construction and infrastructure spending and remains sensitive to economic conditions, while changes in trade policies, duties or sector regulations may impact cost structures and operations. Separately, the Company flags regulatory and compliance risk arising from operating in a regulated environment requiring adherence to SEBI (LODR), taxation and other statutory norms, where non-compliance may result in penalties and reputational impact. The Directors' Report adds a measured FY27 outlook citing geopolitical risks, trade disruptions, soft urban demand and inflationary pressures.

one-line thesis: Second consecutive quarter proving the trading→manufacturing pivot: blended EBITDA margin now >4% (~4.5%), annualized ROCE ~23%, on a net-cash Rs 690 cr balance sheet — with management stressing this is *structural*, not inventory-gain (absolute inventory actually fell to Rs 209 cr from Rs 284 cr despite Rs 2,500-3,000/ton steel-price inflation). The four value-added verticals (service centers, steel profiles, renewable structures, accessories) are being scaled toward a 2030 vision of 4-4.5 mn tons and Rs 25,000-35,000 cr revenue / Rs 1,000 cr+ EBITDA. The margin step-up lever is a Raipur backward-integration (coated-steel) line, operational in ~18 months, taking profile/renewable EBITDA/ton from Rs 3,000-4,000 to Rs 6,000-7,000.

- **FY27 EBITDA ~Rs 300 cr (absolute)** — reaffirmed from Q4 call; only caveat is a macro/geopolitical shock. Absolute EBITDA to grow every quarter (blended EBITDA/ton may wobble on mix).

- **7 new products** to launch over Q2-Q3 FY27 (capacity already in place); new **contract-manufacturing** category — details next quarter.

- **Vision 2030:** 4-4.5 mn tons; revenue Rs 25,000-35,000 cr; EBITDA min Rs 1,000 cr (3-4% margin) — 3 mn t service centers + ~1 mn t profiles/renewables, ~0 t trading.
order book & pipeline: Mostly off-the-shelf (24-48 hr turnaround) except solar structures (project-specific, 2-3 month order book). 2,500+ customers across EPC/industrial/infrastructure; concentration low except solar (top 20-30 EPCs/IPPs). Installed capacity 400,000 t (profiles+renewables) vs 120,000 t run-rate → 3.5-4x headroom. B2B trading kept optional/opportunistic (Q4 was only 17k t; "anyone's guess").
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Service Centers (7 operational):** SME/MSME customers (fabricators, capital goods, EPC, white goods, auto, agri-equipment); 8,000 t/month → ~Rs 40 cr revenue/month → ~Rs 500 cr/yr per center; Rs 50 cr gross-block + Rs 25-30 cr WC = Rs 75-80 cr capital/center → Rs 20 cr EBITDA; 9-15 months to build. ROCE can rise to ~35% once coated steel + B2B trading layer on.
- **Steel Profiles (18k t):** Strut, Z/C Purlins, racking, cable trays — construction/infra/industries; special-coated steel.
- **Renewable Structures (11k t):** solar module-mounting for EPCs/IPPs; capacity 200k t (2-3 yrs of demand headroom).
- **Accessories:** 2 products launched, double-digit margins; ramp begun.
- **B2B Metal Trading:** deliberately subordinate, zero-capital ROCE-booster.
growth verticals / optionality: Raipur coated-steel backward integration (CRM + zinc/zinc-al/zinc-al-mg coating); 7-product Q2-Q3 launch; contract manufacturing (new category, "gap in giving manufacturing ecosystem to brand-owners"); own online marketplace for SG Mart products; B2B trading optionality. Analogized as "China in the making" — multi-product/multi-industry/multi-channel formalization play.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Only pan-India *organized* service-center/profiling network:** competitors are fragmented "mom-and-pop" profilers buying from mills and selling locally; SGMART's edge is pan-India profiling at service centers **+ own backward integration** in coated steel — a combination "no existing player" in solar structures/profiles has. Multi-vertical/multi-channel breadth makes it "very tough for any big entrant."
- **APL Apollo DNA:** management explicitly runs the SG Mart playbook (inventory-churn discipline, minimize P&L inventory noise, value-added spread over volume) from its APL Apollo experience — a credible execution track record.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA/ton hierarchy: Accessories (double-digit %) > Profiles (Rs 3,000-4,000) ≈ Renewables (Rs 3,000-3,500) > Service Centers (Rs 1,800-2,000) > B2B trading. Blended >4% will oscillate with mix (a service-center-heavy quarter dilutes per-ton), but *absolute* EBITDA grows every quarter. Backward integration is the structural margin unlock (+Rs 3,000-4,000/t on profiles/renewables). Group ROCE floor: no vertical below 20%; aspiration >25%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Rs 90 cr Q1; Rs 400-500 cr FY27; Rs 1,500 cr total over 2-3 years — ~Rs 900 cr on 15-18 new service centers (Rs 50 cr each) + Raipur coated-steel line + accessories machinery. Fully funded by Rs 690 cr net cash + operating cash flow; **no capital raise / dilution**. Raipur land acquired, construction begun, some machinery ordered. **Watch:** service-center build cadence (12 within 6-12 months) + Raipur 18-month timeline.
capital allocation: Self-funded growth (net cash + OCF); no equity dilution. Discipline: any new vertical must clear >20% ROCE (contract manufacturing included). Working-capital rationalization (advances to mills to secure supply amid geopolitics) as scale builds.
risks & watch-items:
- **Geopolitics/steel-price volatility:** Iran-US war reignited ~10 days pre-call; oil→steel/commodity volatility; a March-style fuel/gas shortage would hurt customer industries and sales broadly ("nothing specific to us").
- **Coated-steel dependency** on third parties until Raipur commissions (18 months) — execution/slippage risk.
- **Seasonality** in service-center volumes (Q1 QoQ dip).
- **Mix-driven EBITDA/ton variability** (management won't guide per-ton QoQ).
- Rapid multi-vertical expansion execution risk.
management quality / tone: Confident, granular, disclosure-forward (added segmental splits; accepted analyst suggestion to publish per-segment EBITDA). Careful not to over-promise per-ton margins; reframes the "25 vs 30 service centers" target as coverage-of-industrial-clusters rather than a number. Repeatedly anchors credibility to the APL Apollo track record. Candid that a macro shock is the one real caveat to the Rs 300 cr EBITDA guide.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The margin uplift is *real*, not cyclical: absolute inventory fell Rs 284→209 cr into rising steel prices, so there is little inventory-gain flatter in the >4% EBITDA margin.
- Backward integration is the whole thesis — it converts a Rs 3,000-4,000/t bought-coated-steel business into a Rs 6,000-7,000/t integrated one; the 18-month Raipur timeline is the single most important milestone.
- Trading is being deliberately zeroed out of the 2030 volume vision (4 mn t of the target is "0 t trading") — a quality-over-volume signal often missed by those anchoring on the old aggregator model.
- Contract manufacturing (details next quarter) is a new, potentially large optionality not yet in numbers.

hero.oneLiner: SG Mart Limited positions itself as India's Integrated Building & Infrastructure Materials Platform, operating across four business verticals spanning sourcing, processing and distribution of metals and building materials.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SG Mart Limited positions itself as India's Integrated Building & Infrastructure Materials Platform, operating across four business verticals spanning sourcing, processing and distribution of metals and building materials.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SG Mart supplies metals and building materials, including steel products such as hot rolled coils, billets, TMT bars and structural steel, to customers across construction, industrial, infrastructure and manufacturing applications. Operations are organised across four business verticals: B2B metal trading, a network of service centres, Steel Profiling Products and solar structures, allowing participation from bulk sourcing and trading through value-added processing to downstream distribution. The Company procures bulk metal directly from primary producers and supplies dealers, distributors and industrial buyers, supported by a pan-regional network of warehouses and service centres.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- SG Marts FZE — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% of shares held by the listed entity (BRSR Section A item 23). Incorporated on January 24, 2024. Operates an office / processing service centre in Dubai and serves the international locations on behalf of the Company, which itself records nil export contribution. Does not participate in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity. Counterparty in the related-party note for interest income, guarantee commission income, investment in share capital, sales, loans and advances, with a guarantee issued on its behalf.
- SG Super 101 Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% of shares held by the listed entity (BRSR Section A item 23). Incorporated on August 06, 2024. Does not participate in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity. Counterparty in the related-party note for investment in share capital.
- SG Sports & Entertainment Private Limited — related party: Enterprise in which KMP and their relatives are interested. Counterparty in the related-party note for business promotion expense, interest income and loans given/repaid.
- Apollo Pipes Limited — related party: Enterprise in which KMP and their relatives are interested. Counterparty in the related-party note for purchases, sales and trade receivables.
- Mr. Sameer Gupta — related party: Relative of KMP (spouse of Ms. Meenakshi Gupta); personal guarantee given on behalf of the Company.
- Mr. Dhruv Gupta — related party: Relative of KMP (son of Ms. Meenakshi Gupta); personal guarantee given on behalf of the Company.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 EBITDA ~Rs 300 cr (absolute)** — reaffirmed from Q4 call; only caveat is a macro/geopolitical shock. Absolute EBITDA to grow every quarter (blended EBITDA/ton may wobble on mix).
- **Revenue growth ~50% CAGR** over next 3 years (analyst-stated, management-owned as target).
- **Service centers: 25 by 2029** (from 7; +5/yr); **12 operational within 6-12 months** (7 new already under construction, land/cities identified).
- **Raipur backward integration (coated steel): operational in ~18 months** → profile/renewable EBITDA/ton to Rs 6,000-7,000 (from Rs 3,000-4,000); +Rs 3,000-4,000/t uplift.
- **Profiles + renewables: 3.5-4x volume growth** in 2-3 years (120k t run-rate today vs 400k t installed capacity).
- **7 new products** to launch over Q2-Q3 FY27 (capacity already in place); new **contract-manufacturing** category — details next quarter.
- **Working capital: 27 days → 20-25 days** within 2 years (backward integration cuts raw-material stocking).
- **Vision 2030:** 4-4.5 mn tons; revenue Rs 25,000-35,000 cr; EBITDA min Rs 1,000 cr (3-4% margin) — 3 mn t service centers + ~1 mn t profiles/renewables, ~0 t trading.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's construction industry — valued at USD 685 billion in FY 2025 and estimated to reach around USD 1,245.7 billion by FY 2034 (CAGR 6.8%) — driven by sustained government capital expenditure, rising urbanisation and investment in roads, railways, metro projects and energy
- Indian real estate momentum, valued at approximately USD 532.6 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 1.26 trillion by 2034 (CAGR 10%), with increasing traction in Tier II and Tier III cities broadening the demand base
- Structural shift in the Indian B2B building materials market driven by a capital expenditure push and rapid industry formalisation, moving procurement from fragmented local sourcing to organised, high-volume supply chain networks; the infrastructure and construction goods segment recorded double-digit growth of 13.7%
- Rapid digitalisation of B2B trade, with e-commerce accounting for nearly 30% of contractor order volumes and buyers moving to unified digital platforms prioritising pricing transparency and multi-warehouse inventory management
- Renewable energy expansion — India crossing over 50% non-fossil-fuel installed power capacity ahead of its 2030 targets, with a record 55.29 GW added during FY 2025-26 — supporting demand for solar mounting structures
- Indian steel industry growth, with crude steel production at 168.4 million tonnes (up 10.7%) and consumption at 163.7 million tonnes (up 7.6%) in FY 2025-26, supported by infrastructure, construction and manufacturing demand
- Government capital expenditure allocation of approximately INR 12.2 lakh crore (about 3.1% of GDP) in the Union Budget FY 2025-26, accelerating investment under PM GatiShakti and the National Infrastructure Pipeline
- Margin lever from progressively rebalancing the business mix towards higher-margin value-added and application-driven segments (service centres, steel profiling, solar structures) and away from low-margin B2B trading
- B2B metal trading demand remained robust with stronger momentum observed in the second half of the year, though segment volumes and revenues stabilised at lower levels reflecting a calibrated trading approach
- Management flags a measured outlook: FY27 growth projected at 6.8%-7.2%, with geopolitical risks, trade disruptions, soft urban demand and inflationary pressures as watch items, alongside input cost volatility and cyclical demand fluctuations
- Solar structures: strengthened relationships with EPC firms and IPPs, reflected in repeat orders and a steadily expanding network within this segment
- Steel Profiling Products: distributor engagement strengthened through branding support and facilitation of project approvals, enhancing order visibility and market responsiveness
- Service centres: order fulfilment processes strengthened through defined service lead times and SAP-based production and inventory management, improving visibility and control over order execution
- No quantified order book or order-inflow value is disclosed in this section

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SG Mart operates a pan-regional network of warehouses and service centres, with 7 operational service centres and 7,200+ SKUs as disclosed in the MD&A company overview. The Directors' Report states the Company plans to add three to four additional centres in FY27, with opportunities actively being evaluated in Hyderabad, Chennai and Punjab. Alongside the service centre build-out, the Company is expanding into application-led segments such as solar structures and steel profiles, and is undertaking backward integration initiatives including zinc coating to enhance value realisation. In the Steel Profiling Products vertical the stated intent is to scale capacity to 0.5 MTPA alongside further expansion of the distribution network and deeper engagement with channel partners, having transitioned that vertical from a trading-led model to a white-labelling and franchise-based royalty model with increased franchise onboarding during the year. In solar structures, the Company expanded its presence into rooftop solar structures and established a distribution network, operates in-house manufacturing capabilities across locations supported by advanced machinery and dedicated in-house tooling workshops, and aims to expand capacity up to 0.5 MTPA through ongoing capacity additions, scaling its presence significantly over the next two to three years. The MD&A strengths and opportunities commentary cites ongoing addition of service centres across geographies as an opportunity expected to improve volumes and operating leverage, and notes that a strong capital base supports expansion of service centres, capacity addition and working capital needs. Separately, the BRSR Principle 2 disclosure states the Company made capital investments in rainwater harvesting systems, alcohol breath analysers, fire safety equipment and water purification systems; such sustainability-linked capex was 0.04% of total capex in FY 2025-26 versus 0.2% in FY 2024-25. No rupee quantum for the overall capex programme is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

- In-house manufacturing and tooling capability in solar structures, giving control over production, quality and turnaround times, with repeat orders from EPC firms and IPPs
